title: AdvantageS of vIdeolaryngoscopy in infanTs undergoing Elective General Anesthesia
summary: In this study, the care of infants with a breathing tube (intubation) is to be examined in more detail. In some operations and interventions, intubation cannot be dispensed with. However, performing intubation requires a lot of practice and it is even more difficult to achieve this level of expertise, especially with the smallest patients. A laryngoscope is required to perform intubation in order to visualize the area of the vocal cords and thus the entrance to the trachea. Therefore, this study will compare a conventional laryngoscope without the possibility of video visualization with a video laryngoscope. The main aim is to see which device enables faster intubation. In addition, it should also be shown whether there are fewer injuries and falling oxygen saturations during intubation. This has already been demonstrated in adults. Comparable data in infants are only insufficiently available.
conditions: Device comparison of different laryngoscopes in infants.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All infants in the Pediatric Clinic, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery and Eye Clinic
Consent of the legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal of the custodian
Age < 28 days or > 1 year
Tracheostoma care
Predictably difficult airway (syndromes, craniofacial dysmorphia, jaw clamping)
